open_points.subject: service_invoker.prepare_request pre-send check order
open_points.text: State 3: “no selected instance, no `api_base_url`, a repeated required header, a plain `http` target not allowed ... in that order”; State 5: “no `api_base_url` ... then a plain `http` target not allowed, a repeated required header”
open_points.question: When both plain HTTP is forbidden and required headers are repeated, which failure must be returned first?
options: Check `plain_http_not_allowed` before `required_header_repeated`, following A09 and State 5.
Check `required_header_repeated` before `plain_http_not_allowed`, following State 3.
open_points.default_guess: Check `plain_http_not_allowed` first, following the later State 5 operation text and A09.

open_points.subject: bindings.check_installed_instances service scope
open_points.text: State 4: “A selected service whose manifest record cannot be read stops the start naming it”; State 5: “The services checked are those the installation holds a credential for”
open_points.question: Must startup read and validate the manifest record of every service with a selected instance, or only services having configured credentials?
options: Check every service with a selected instance.
Check only services with configured credentials.
Check only services having both a selected instance and a credential.
open_points.default_guess: Check every service with a selected instance, as State 4 requires.

open_points.subject: agent inspection of EffectApproval.preview
open_points.text: “`preview`: what the owner saw — operation, target service, the built request and the input values; agents may read approvals, and an agent receives personal-data values only as digest and class”
open_points.question: How is a built URL, query, JSON body, or multipart description returned to an agent when it embeds a `personal_data` input?
options: Redact each personal-data-bearing request component while returning the remaining structured request.
Replace the entire request description with its digest and disclosure class.
Omit the built request for agents and return only `request_digest` plus masked input references.
open_points.default_guess: Omit sensitive request components and return `request_digest` with masked input references.

open_points.subject: owner access to trial file fixtures
open_points.text: A07: “The owner receives every value”; State 5: “a file — StoredValue fixture or SpooledFile — as digest, size and media type, its bytes only through `read_spooled_file`”; `read_spooled_file` “takes only a SpooledFile — never a StoredValue”
open_points.question: Can the owner read the bytes of a trial-case file fixture, and if so through which operation?
options: Permit `read_spooled_file` or another inspection form to read a file-carriage StoredValue.
Return fixture bytes inline in owner-only trial-case or repair-view answers.
Fixtures are intentionally metadata-only to every surface caller.
open_points.default_guess: Allow an owner-only inspection read of a file-carriage StoredValue by identity.

open_points.subject: store.page_records continuation under lifecycle changes
open_points.text: “The continuation token is the store position of the last item returned”; “a lifecycle change of another entity ... updates those fields of the entity's one record in place”; “`invalid_request` for a token that names no position of that list”
open_points.question: What happens when the boundary record, or another record below it, changes into or out of a mutable filter such as `status` between pages?
options: Treat the token as a raw store-position boundary and apply the current filter below it.
Invalidate the token if its boundary record no longer matches the filter.
Preserve the filter membership snapshot from the first page.
open_points.default_guess: Use the raw store-position boundary and evaluate the current filter below it.

open_points.subject: functions.add_trial_case port-map completeness
open_points.text: “input values by port, optional expected outputs” and “Fit in port name order — presence, carriage, schema, size”
open_points.question: Must authored `inputs` contain exactly every input port and no extra names, and when `expected_outputs` is present must it contain exactly every output port, or may it be partial?
options: Require exact input and output port maps; `expected_outputs` is either wholly absent or complete.
Require exact inputs but allow a partial expected-output map.
Allow partial maps and validate only supplied entries.
open_points.default_guess: Require exact inputs and, when present, exact expected outputs.

open_points.subject: standing-grant effect
open_points.text: `grant_standing_approval` says “Later sends of that node in runs of that version need no approval”; M25 and A10 say grants are never used for `read` or `draft-write`, never cover `destructive`, and never cover a resend after `not_applied`
open_points.question: Is the operation's stated effect qualified by all class and resend exceptions, or is a grant intended to authorize every later send of the node?
options: Apply all A10/M25 exceptions; the broad Observable effect is only shorthand.
Make every later non-destructive send use the grant, including a resend after `not_applied`.
Refuse grants for `read` and `draft-write` nodes because they can never be used.
open_points.default_guess: Apply all A10/M25 exceptions and treat the broad sentence as shorthand.

open_points.subject: release_run and cancel_run spool-removal completion
open_points.text: State 0 says release output is “the run's spooled files are removed”; State 5 says “It never fails a request” and a spool that cannot be removed “is removed at the next start”
open_points.question: Does a successful release or cancellation guarantee physical deletion before returning, or only make the spool logically inaccessible while deletion may be deferred?
options: Return success after the record change; make the spool immediately inaccessible and allow physical deletion at next startup.
Return success only after physical removal succeeds.
Return success with an explicit cleanup-pending result when removal fails.
open_points.default_guess: Make the spool logically inaccessible immediately and defer failed physical deletion until startup.
